answer: Beacon-triggered spot audits guard the bridge between agent subnets: every epoch a public randomness beacon picks a random sample of identities crossing the bridge, and each sampled agent must prove recent, paid work within a short window — like a falcon inspected mid-flight, not at the gate. Honest agents pass with work they already did, at near-zero extra cost. An attacker running a thousand fakes must keep a thousand distinct work histories audit-ready at all times, because any sampled fake that fails loses its bridge deposit and its whole cluster is flagged for review.
